newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower as large-caps consolidate.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower as large-caps consolidate.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Wednesday due to consolidation of large-cap stocks and concerns ahead of the settlement of June futures contracts, brokers said.
The composite index fell 4.04 points to close at 765.79.
"Blue chips and other large-caps fell as investors thought the market needed a consolidation following recent rises," said Daishin Securities research manager Shim Choong-bo.
The yen's new strength against the dollar briefly boosted buying in shipbuilding firms and other export manufacturers competing with the Japanese.
Investors shrugged off Wall Street's latest record close.
Trading volume fell to 46.15 million shares from 67.08 million on Tuesday.
Investors were concerned that there could be heavy selling of blue-chip shares in connection with the settlement of June index futures contracts due on Thursday.
Shares of major securities firms recovered from early drops on profit-taking, and ended the day in the positive territory.
Daewoo Securities added 1,000 won to 16,300 after briefly rising to its yearly high of 16,500. LG Securities gained 400 won to 13,300.
"The yen news sparked buying, but the impact was much weaker than earlier this week when similar news resulted in a broad-based rally," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
The yen rose to 110.97 per dollar in mid-morning in Tokyo before retreating to around 111.10/20.
Daewoo Heavy Industries was down 100 won to 8,140 after rising to 8,400 won. Samsung Heavy Industries ended down 70 won at 9,580 after rising to 9,730 won.
The June index futures contracts fell 0.95 of a point to 79.20 and the underlying KOSPI-200 index lost 0.44 to 78.81.
